summary: Will B. Miller works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Janet Gyatso, and also studied under Lopen Chorten in 2012.

Will Sweetman works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Cambridge (~1992–1993) and Lancaster University (~1993–1997), and held a post at the University of Otago around 2003.

Willard Gurdon Oxtoby was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tamalpais High School, Stanford University, Princeton University, and Harvard University. He held a post at the University of Toronto from around 1971 to 1999.
Willard J. Peterson is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology who was mentored by Denis Twitchett. He served as a professor at Princeton University (attested 1981).

Willard Van Orman Quine was a philosopher and linguist educated at Oberlin College and Harvard University. He served in the U.S. Navy (1942–1945) and held posts at Harvard University (professor, 1933–1978) and Wesleyan University (1964–1965).

Willem Bollée was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University and the University of Hamburg. He was an assistant professor at the University of Münster (1971–1978) and a lecturer and professor at Heidelberg University.

Willem Caland was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Leiden University (~1877–1882). He held posts at Utrecht University (1906–1917 as Professor of Sanskrit; ~1906–1929 as Chair of Sanskrit) and Leiden University (1913–1914).

Willem van der Molen is a scholar of linguistics, history/archaeology, and Indology who studied at Leiden University (~1970–1983). He held posts at Leiden University (~1978–2017) and the University of Indonesia.
William C. Kirby is a Sinologist and historian who studied at Dartmouth College (~1968–1972) and Harvard University (~1972–1981). He held a post at Harvard University around 1992.

William Carey was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Golok Nath Sharma (~1796–1801). He founded the Serampore Mission Press and was appointed Professor of Sanscrit, &c., at Fort William College in 1801.

William Chu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the University of California, Los Angeles by 2006. He studied under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr. and committee member William M. Bodiford.

William Dwight Whitney was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Williams, Yale, Berlin, and Tübingen. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Yale (1853–1894) and held offices in the American Oriental Society.

William Edelglass is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. He has taught philosophy at Colby College (attested 2007), was a professor at Marlboro College (attested 2013), and served as a visiting professor at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.
William Erskine was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at the Royal High School and studied at the University of Edinburgh from around 1788 to 1792.
William Frederic Sinclair was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Royal School, Armagh, and entered the Indian Civil Service in 1866.

William H. Nienhauser, Jr. is a Sinologist who studied at Indiana University and the University of Bonn under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Alexander Bischoff. He has held faculty posts, including Halls-Bascom Professor, at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
William J. Johnson is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He has held academic posts at Cardiff University and the University of Wales (attested 1998).

William James was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Plymouth College and Harvard University, including its Medical School and School of Engineering. He held an academic post at Harvard University from around 1872 to 1907.

William Jones was an Indologist and linguist educated at Harrow School and University College, Oxford. In 1783, he became Chief Justice at the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William, and in 1784 founded the Asiatic Society.

William L. Ames is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar educated at Caltech and the University of Washington under Collett Cox and David Seyfort Ruegg. He held posts at Washington, CIIS, and JFK University (librarian, attested 2006).
